Package io.webagent4j.recording

Record Class WorkflowRecording

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
io.webagent4j.recording.WorkflowRecording
Record Components:
schemaVersion - the canonical JSON schema version this recording conforms to
recordingId - the non-sensitive caller-supplied recording identifier, persisted verbatim and ignored by WorkflowReplayVerifier
capturedAt - the caller-supplied capture time, ignored by WorkflowReplayVerifier
workflowId - the recorded execution's workflow identifier
status - the recorded execution's overall terminal outcome
steps - every step's recorded outcome, in workflow definition order
failure - the overall recorded failure, present exactly when status is WorkflowStatus.FAILED
public record WorkflowRecording(RecordingSchemaVersion schemaVersion, RecordingId recordingId, Instant capturedAt, WorkflowId workflowId, WorkflowStatus status, List<RecordedWorkflowStep> steps, Optional<RecordedFailure> failure) extends Record
An immutable, versioned recording that excludes raw workflow values and preserves engine-redacted diagnostics.

A recording is data, not a program: it has no execute() method, retains no action factory, prepared action plan, page, or browser reference, and cannot replay itself. Replaying a recording means asking WorkflowReplayVerifier to compare it against a caller-supplied WorkflowResult from a new, independently performed execution - never deserializing this type to automatically click, type, submit, or navigate again. See docs/recording.md for the full architecture and the rationale for what is and is not recorded.

recordingId and capturedAt are always caller-supplied, exactly like WorkflowId: neither is generated inside this module, so the same recording data always produces the same identity and timestamp regardless of how many times it is captured or re-encoded. Identifiers such as recordingId and an action's actionId are persisted verbatim, are visible through record toString() output, and must contain only non-sensitive metadata.
